newsitem.title: USA: U.S. T-bond futures seen catching breath.
newsitem.headline: U.S. T-bond futures seen catching breath.

text.p: U.S. Treasury bond futures were likely to catch their breath for a few days after strong advances in recent weeks, technical analysts said.
"For the next few days, probably some consolidation is in order," said Larry Berman, senior technical analyst at Technical Data.
"We had some bullish data and we weren't able to extend the market any," he said, referring the market's reaction to today's October U.S. producer price index (PPI).
December T-bond futures were down about half a point at midsession at around 114-1/2.

He added this correction in the intraday momentum indicators should run its course by late Friday or Monday. He also pointed out that down moves in short-term stochastics were not solid on an uptrend and could end abruptly.
Even as the market consolidates, Grauer noted, the monthly stochastic, which had downcrossed in March after the market topped out in January, was coming closer to upcrossing again.
"I'm quite confident that this will cross in the next 15 days," he said. "That will end this secular (long-term) bear market."
Still, he cautioned, there could be another consolidation of 20 days or so after the expected near-term bounce, given the daily stochastic was starting to look toppish.
At the shorter end of the yield curve, Berman at Technical Data said Eurodollar futures were unlikely to move out of recent ranges.
A Nov 1 high of 94.51 in March Eurodollars should hold for at least a few more weeks, he said.
